 Bournemouth's Scott and Kroupi ready to start, says Rose
 AFC Bournemouth 
 Football 
 Sport 
 By 
 Alexander Smith
 Senior sports reporter 
 Share
 0 Comments 
 (Image: Richard Crease) 
 This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today,
 and has been written by our American colleagues.
 It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.
 ALEX Scott and Junior Kroupi are both ready to start for the Cherries , Marco Rose has confirmed.
 Scott and Kroupi both returned from injury before the international break, with Kroupi getting some valuable minutes off the bench for Bournemouth in the four games he was available for before the interval.
 The Englishman, meanwhile, was on the bench for the trip to Ipswich two weeks ago, but he did not come on, although it was the plan to give him minutes in Suffolk.

 Before the international window, Rose said the hope was to use the two weeks to get both players fit to feature more once club football returned.
 He confirmed that they had been able to do that with Scott, but Kroupi was a late call-up to the France national side, where he made his debut for Les Bleus and scored his first goal for his country.
 (Image: PA) 
 Bournemouth went into the break in top form and with plenty of momentum, but Rose was happy to have a bit of a break before Saturday's visit of Nottingham Forest.
 Rose said: “Some players in the squad had some more good training sessions with some players that came back: Alex Scott, Junior Kroupi.
 “Okay, Junior went to the national team after two days, but everyone came back healthy from the international break and today we were the first time with the whole group together.
 “Now we just start again.”
 The German boss confirmed that it is the plan for Scott to start in one of the next three games, against Nottingham Forest, Celta Vigo and Fulham.
 (Image: Andrew Matthews/PA Wire) 
 He said: “We're going to see what we do, but we have many games in the upcoming weeks and even next week three games.
 “So a lot of choices and for sure he's going to start in one game of this.
 “We have to increase the match time step by step, but he had a good two weeks with training and some rest.
 “Now I think Alex is ready, Junior's ready to get more match time and even to start.”
 Rose also confirmed that he had no wider concerns, with the squad in a good position heading into a very busy period.
 (Image: Richard Crease) 
 He said: “The only worries I have or concerns or considerations is that I need to make choices and have to make decisions.
 “It means some tough talks maybe, but on the other side, again, we have so many games and the lads already showed that I can trust everyone in this squad.
 “So everyone is going to get his time to show up, his time to play.
 “It's just good to have them back, to have the quality, to have competition in the team.
 “Even these two guys, because we really played well the last eight games, need to perform to stay part of the team.”
